I will do it much like last year, just a little tighter on the money where I can. I have 40 mu, and all of it runs wheat and maize in turn, so the same 40 mu goes into wheat first and then maize after harvest. I do not like cutting fertilizer too hard. If the crop turns weak, I cannot make that yield back later. Around here, if the neighbors put on close to 1 bag more, I would rather follow that than be short. On wheat, I will use a full base fertilizer and then chase it once with nitrogen when it starts growing strong in spring. With my well, I can give wheat 3 waters if the year is normal. On maize, I will sow a hybrid because that is what people around me use when they want grain, and I will feed it heavier than wheat because maize eats a lot. I will give maize 2 waters in a normal year, and I will not skip spray if I see worms or disease starting. For tillage, I will use rotary tillage. On 40 mu, that is faster and cheaper than deep ploughing every time, and I can finish on time between wheat and maize.
